reason: This two-provider variant requires both Claude and Cursor timing lanes; the tester requested Claude-only QA. The Claude lane was observed, but Cursor was not run. No live worker-fault fixture was authorized or applied, so the harmless command exit is not evidence of runner failure.
observations: One fresh QA Claude conversation ran the harmless command false, which exited 1, and gave a normal reply. The first workspace was created at 05:31:38.595 UTC and handed off at 05:31:51.117 UTC; the reply was visible by 05:32:09.950 UTC. The nonzero command result was expected application behavior, not an Agent-Relay worker failure.

The first runner was serving at a clearly pre-follow-up T+9 sample ending 05:41:17.982 UTC. Enter for one same-session follow-up was bounded to 05:41:35.662 to 05:41:46.167 UTC, before the earliest possible original idle release. It replied by 05:41:59.144 UTC. The same runner still served at 05:52:00.444, beyond ten minutes even from that latest reply observation. Relay observed clean done 0 at 05:52:09.723, queued natural deletion at 05:52:10.243, and the workspace was absent by 05:52:31.799. Actual worker exit time is unknown.

The same privately correlated Claude session paused and later resumed on a new QA workspace created at 05:55:53.573 UTC. A normal reply visible by 05:56:24.742 recalled the earlier command result. That second workspace remained serving through 06:06:24.920, then exited cleanly, was queued for natural deletion at 06:06:46.545 and was absent by 06:07:26.944. The browser showed paused again by 06:08:05.459; no manual stop, restart, config change or forced worker fault occurred.

Four visually reviewed reply/paused-state crops and a ten-event field-restricted Relay log excerpt are public evidence. Original viewports and the ten-line raw Relay source-log archive remain private. Browser Enter and reply times are bounded observations, not invented precise occurrence times; a separate local image-viewer tab briefly obscured the first post-resume browser sample.
